visual.general_description: Procedural workflow collage of SBRT planning and delivery in four stages.
visual.detailed_description: Collage with four red-outlined column headings (CT simulation, VT substrate confirm, QA, Treatment) joined by three blue block arrows. Under CT simulation are two tiles labelled Fixation with vacuum-assisted device (a photograph of a person lying on a CT couch with white adhesive patches and wires on the chest and a blue bar over the eye region only, leaving the lower face visible) and Four-dimensional CT simulation (a chest scan screen). Under VT substrate confirm are four tiles: CARTO 3D mapping (a colored chamber map), Image fusion with MRI and CT (two fused cross-sections with outlines), Image fusion with MRI, CT and 99mTc-sestamibi (two colored short-axis style displays) and Target delineation (a CT view with a red-boxed Target label and a red arrow to a blue-shaded region). Under QA is one photograph labelled Quality assurance check showing a linear accelerator. Under Treatment are four tiles: Localization by image-guided system (a screen with three CT views and a settings panel), SARS delivery (a person lying under a linear accelerator with a blue bar over the eye region), Real time monitor during delivery (a camera view of the treatment room with a person under blue drapes and a camera stamp at the top right), and Treatment completed (a group of people in white coats, most wearing masks, with colored overlays over the eye areas; the gowned person among them is not masked and the lower face is visible).

caption_claims.value: Multimodal imaging with scar imaging, CT, MRI and sestamibi MPI was used offline to delineate a target; QA was performed one day before treatment; on the day of treatment the patient was immobilized on a vacuum device, CBCT was used for setup and 12 Gy was delivered by VMAT.

evidence.quote: Multimodal imaging combined with scar imaging, including the CARTO mapping system (Biosense, Diamond Bar, CA), CT, MRI and ^(99)^(m)Tc-sestamibi MPI, was used offline to delineate a target for ablation. A plan was developed in the Pinnacle3 planning system (version 9.8.1, Philips Medical Systems, Madison, WI, USA). One day before treatment, quality assurance was performed. On the day of treatment, the patient was immobilized on the vacuum device, and cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) was used for patient setup and target localization. The treatment unit was aligned with the patient, and a dose of 12 Gy was delivered precisely by volumetric-modulated arc therapy (VMAT) through a linear accelerator machine (Versa HDTM, Elekta, Crawley, West Sussex, UK) with 6 MV photons.
